title: Antisymmetry of monotone maps
statement: For maps $M,M' : \mathbb{Z} \to \{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, suppose every integer at which $M$ is true is also one at which $M'$ is true, and conversely. Then $M=M'$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a function from integers to Booleans
M' is a function from integers to Booleans
M is pointwise included in M'
M' is pointwise included in M
